title: Dollar Stores Are the Most Expensive Store in America
hook: Fifty-four million Americans shop dollar stores every week to save money — but per ounce, per use, per serving, it's one of the most expensive places you can shop.
angle: Contrarian: dollar stores feel cheap but deliberately sell tiny packages to trigger unit-price blindness — the per-unit cost is 3-4x higher than bulk alternatives, and they cluster in low-income neighborhoods with fewest alternatives
audience: Budget shoppers, low-to-middle income earners, and deal hunters who don't realize the $1.25 sticker hides one of retail's highest per-unit markups
key_numbers: 22¢/oz dollar store detergent vs. 6¢/oz at Costco — nearly 4x more expensive
36,000 dollar stores in the US — more than McDonald's and Starbucks combined
73% of dollar stores located in lower-income neighborhoods
$1,400/year overspend vs. buying equivalent bulk products
$140,000 over a working life — invested at 7% it's even more
